comments.author: @francoUSAhome
comments.text:
Geoff, genuine question: Why do you still rely so heavily on the Mercator projection in your videos? Given how much you educate people about geography, wouldn't it make sense to use a projection that better represents the actual relative sizes of countries and continents?

The Mercator projection dramatically distorts landmass sizes, especially at higher latitudes. Greenland, for example, appears almost as large as Africa on a Mercator map, when in reality Africa is roughly 14 times larger. South America is also vastly larger than Greenland, despite what many familiar world maps suggest.

Even Google Earth makes this obvious when you switch to the globe view rather than looking at a flat map.

The UN has also addressed this issue: in 2017, the United Nations adopted a resolution promoting the use of the Equal Earth projection for depicting the world more accurately in certain contexts.

Wouldn't using equal-area projections, such as Equal Earth or Gall-Peters, be a great opportunity to educate your audience about how the maps we grow up seeing can distort our perception of the world?
